definitions.explanation: A physical measure of how much light bends, or slows, when it passes into a material. A higher value means light is refracted more strongly.

examples.japanese: ⟦ガラス→ガラス：01777_garasu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{屈折率|くっせつりつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{測|はか}る→測る：01977_hakaru⟧。
examples.english: To measure the refractive index of glass.

examples.japanese: ⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦ガラス→ガラス：01777_garasu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{屈折率|くっせつりつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧。
examples.english: Water and glass have different refractive indices.

examples.japanese: ⟦レンズ→レンズ：07808_renzu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{設計|せっけい}→設計：03300_sekkei⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{材料|ざいりょう}→材料：02831_zairyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{屈折率|くっせつりつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{重要|じゅうよう}→重要：01575_juuyou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: In lens design, the refractive index of the material is important.

notes:
A physics term expressing how strongly a transparent medium bends light relative to a vacuum. Diamonds appear brilliant because of their very high refractive index.
